### Step P10-005: Backup Automation Full Test

**Type:** Testing
**Status:** Not Started
**Risk:** High
**Git Commit:** `feat(P10): pending`

**Goal:** End-to-end backup test: full backup to both S3 (idcloudhost) and R2 (Cloudflare), restore verification, and data integrity check validating the dual-provider backup strategy under real conditions.
**Dependencies:** P0 backup scripts operational (restic + pg_dump + redis-cli BGSAVE), S3 credentials configured for idcloudhost Jakarta, R2 credentials configured for Cloudflare, SOPS+age keys available for decryption verification.
**Cost Impact:** $2-5/month (S3 storage ~$0.02/GB + R2 storage ~$0.015/GB, estimated 5-10GB total)
**ADR References:** ADR-025 (Backup Strategy), ADR-032 (Dual-Provider Backup — idcloudhost S3 primary + Cloudflare R2 secondary)
**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-OPS-003 (Backup completes within RTO of 4 hours, restore verified), AC-DATA-006 (Restored data respects deletion/do-not-recall obligations)
**Estimated Time:** 4 hours

#### Context

Dual-provider backup strategy per ADR-032: idcloudhost S3 (primary, Jakarta region — low latency) + Cloudflare R2 (secondary, global — geographic diversity). Backup includes: PostgreSQL dump (pg_dump -Fc), Redis dump (BGSAVE .rdb), configuration files (/etc/guinevere, /etc/systemd/system/guinevere-*), secrets encrypted via SOPS+age, application code (git — already on GitHub, backup as secondary copy), and evidence files. Must verify: backup completeness (no missing files), encryption at rest (age headers present), restore within RTO (target < 2 hours, hard limit 4 hours per AC-OPS-003), data integrity (pg_restore with checksums, Redis key counts match), and deletion/do-not-recall obligations honored during restore (AC-DATA-006). Test restore MUST use separate directory/instance — never overwrite production data.

#### Pre-flight Checks
- [ ] S3 credentials configured: `aws s3 ls s3://guinevere-backups/ --endpoint-url https://s3.idcloudhost.com` (or rclone equivalent)
- [ ] R2 credentials configured: `rclone lsd r2:guinevere-backups/` (or aws s3 ls equivalent)
- [ ] SOPS+age keys available: `sops --version && age-keygen --version`
- [ ] PostgreSQL running with data to back up: `psql -U guinevere -h localhost -d guinevere -c "SELECT count(*) FROM financial.transactions"`
- [ ] Redis running with data to back up: `redis-cli -p 6380 DBSIZE`
- [ ] Test restore directory exists and empty: `mkdir -p /tmp/guinevere-restore-test && ls /tmp/guinevere-restore-test/`
- [ ] Sufficient disk space for test restore: `df -h /tmp` (need 2x backup size)
- [ ] Backup scripts executable: `ls -la /opt/guinevere/scripts/backup*.sh`

#### Commands

```bash
# 1. Document test start time and backup metadata
echo "BACKUP_TEST_START=$(date -Iseconds)" \
  > docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt
echo "PG_ROWS_BEFORE=$(psql -U guinevere -h localhost -d guinevere -t -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM financial.transactions')" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt
echo "REDIS_KEYS_BEFORE=$(redis-cli -p 6380 DBSIZE)" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt

# 2. Trigger full PostgreSQL dump (custom format with compression)
pg_dump -U guinevere -h localhost -d guinevere \
  -Fc --no-owner --no-acl --verbose \
  -f /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/postgresql-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).dump \
  2>&1 | tee docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/pgdump-output.txt
PG_DUMP_SIZE=$(stat --format=%s /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/postgresql-*.dump)
echo "PG_DUMP_SIZE_BYTES=${PG_DUMP_SIZE}" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt

# 3. Trigger Redis BGSAVE (non-blocking snapshot)
redis-cli -p 6380 BGSAVE
# Wait for BGSAVE to complete (check lastsave changes)
sleep 5
while redis-cli -p 6380 INFO persistence | grep -q "rdb_bgsave_in_progress:1"; do
  echo "Waiting for Redis BGSAVE to complete..."
  sleep 2
done
# Copy the RDB file to backup directory
cp /var/lib/redis/dump.rdb \
  /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/redis-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).rdb
REDIS_DUMP_SIZE=$(stat --format=%s /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/redis-*.rdb)
echo "REDIS_DUMP_SIZE_BYTES=${REDIS_DUMP_SIZE}" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt

# 4. Backup configuration files and secrets (tar + SOPS encrypt)
tar -czf /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/configs-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz \
  /etc/guinevere/ \
  /etc/systemd/system/guinevere-* \
  /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini \
  /etc/redis/redis.conf
# Encrypt the config tarball with SOPS+age
sops --encrypt --age $(grep "public key: age" .sops.yaml | head -1 | awk '{print $4}') \
  /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/configs-*.tar.gz \
  > /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/configs-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz.enc
CONFIG_SIZE=$(stat --format=%s /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/configs-*.tar.gz.enc)
echo "CONFIG_ENCRYPTED_SIZE_BYTES=${CONFIG_SIZE}" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt

# 5. Upload to S3 (idcloudhost — primary)
aws s3 sync /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/ \
  s3://guinevere-backups/full-test-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.idcloudhost.com \
  --storage-class STANDARD \
  2>&1 | tee docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/s3-upload-output.txt

# 6. Upload to R2 (Cloudflare — secondary)
rclone sync /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/ \
  r2:guinevere-backups/full-test-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ \
  --progress \
  2>&1 | tee docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/r2-upload-output.txt

# 7. Verify S3 upload — list objects
aws s3 ls s3://guinevere-backups/full-test-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.idcloudhost.com \
  --recursive \
  > docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/s3-verify.txt

# 8. Verify R2 upload — list objects
rclone ls r2:guinevere-backups/full-test-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ \
  > docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/r2-verify.txt

# 9. Encryption verification — check file headers for age encryption markers
for encfile in /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/*.enc; do
  echo "=== $encfile ===" >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/encryption-verify.txt
  head -c 100 "$encfile" | xxd | head -5 \
    >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/encryption-verify.txt
  # Should show "age-encryption.org/v1" in the header
done

# 10. RESTORE TO TEST DIRECTORY (never production)
RESTORE_DIR="/tmp/guinevere-restore-test"
mkdir -p "${RESTORE_DIR}/pgdata" "${RESTORE_DIR}/redis" "${RESTORE_DIR}/configs"

# 10a. Restore PostgreSQL to test directory (requires temp PG instance)
#     Use a temporary PostgreSQL cluster to avoid impacting production
export PGDATA="${RESTORE_DIR}/pgdata"
initdb -D "${PGDATA}" --username=guinevere
pg_ctl -D "${PGDATA}" -l "${RESTORE_DIR}/pg-restore.log" start -o "-p 5433"
sleep 3
# Create database and extensions
createdb -p 5433 -U guinevere guinevere_restore
psql -p 5433 -U guinevere -d guinevere_restore \
  -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb"
psql -p 5433 -U guinevere -d guinevere_restore \
  -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector"
# Restore the dump
pg_restore -p 5433 -U guinevere -d guinevere_restore \
  --verbose --no-owner --no-acl \
  /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/postgresql-*.dump \
  2>&1 | tee docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/pg-restore-output.txt

# 10b. Data integrity check — row counts match pre-backup
PG_ROWS_AFTER=$(psql -p 5433 -U guinevere -d guinevere_restore \
  -t -c "SELECT count(*) FROM financial.transactions")
echo "PG_ROWS_AFTER=${PG_ROWS_AFTER}" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt
PG_ROWS_BEFORE=$(grep PG_ROWS_BEFORE docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt | cut -d'=' -f2)
if [ "$PG_ROWS_BEFORE" = "$PG_ROWS_AFTER" ]; then
  echo "PASS: PostgreSQL row count matches (${PG_ROWS_BEFORE} rows)"
else
  echo "FAIL: PostgreSQL row count mismatch (before: ${PG_ROWS_BEFORE}, after: ${PG_ROWS_AFTER})"
fi

# 10c. Check table-level row counts for key tables
for table in financial.transactions financial.project_costs surveillance.events memory.conversations; do
  COUNT=$(psql -p 5433 -U guinevere -d guinevere_restore -t -c "SELECT count(*) FROM ${table}" 2>/dev/null || echo "TABLE_NOT_FOUND")
  echo "${table}: ${COUNT}" >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/table-row-counts.txt
done

# 10d. Restore Redis to test instance (separate port)
redis-server --port 6381 --dir "${RESTORE_DIR}/redis" --daemonize yes
sleep 2
# Copy RDB into test Redis dir and restart
cp /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/redis-*.rdb "${RESTORE_DIR}/redis/dump.rdb"
redis-cli -p 6381 SHUTDOWN NOSAVE
redis-server --port 6381 --dir "${RESTORE_DIR}/redis" --daemonize yes
sleep 2
REDIS_KEYS_AFTER=$(redis-cli -p 6381 DBSIZE)
REDIS_KEYS_BEFORE=$(grep REDIS_KEYS_BEFORE docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt | cut -d'=' -f2)
echo "REDIS_KEYS_AFTER=${REDIS_KEYS_AFTER}" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt
if [ "$REDIS_KEYS_BEFORE" = "$REDIS_KEYS_AFTER" ]; then
  echo "PASS: Redis key count matches (${REDIS_KEYS_BEFORE} keys)"
else
  echo "FAIL: Redis key count mismatch (before: ${REDIS_KEYS_BEFORE}, after: ${REDIS_KEYS_AFTER})"
fi

# 10e. Configuration file diff — original vs restored
sops --decrypt /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/configs-*.tar.gz.enc \
  > "${RESTORE_DIR}/configs/restored-configs.tar.gz"
tar -xzf "${RESTORE_DIR}/configs/restored-configs.tar.gz" -C "${RESTORE_DIR}/configs/"
diff -r /etc/guinevere/ "${RESTORE_DIR}/configs/etc/guinevere/" \
  > docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/config-diff.txt 2>&1
# Diff should be empty (configs unchanged between backup and restore)

# 11. Cleanup test instances
redis-cli -p 6381 SHUTDOWN NOSAVE
pg_ctl -D "${PGDATA}" stop
echo "BACKUP_TEST_END=$(date -Iseconds)" \
  >> docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt

# 12. Calculate backup size and duration metrics
START_TS=$(grep BACKUP_TEST_START docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt | cut -d'=' -f2)
END_TS=$(grep BACKUP_TEST_END docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt | cut -d'=' -f2)
echo "TOTAL_DURATION: $(($(date -d "$END_TS" +%s) - $(date -d "$START_TS" +%s))) seconds"
echo "TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE: $(du -sh /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/ | cut -f1)"
echo "PG_DUMP_SIZE: $(grep PG_DUMP_SIZE_BYTES docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt | cut -d'=' -f2) bytes"
echo "REDIS_DUMP_SIZE: $(grep REDIS_DUMP_SIZE_BYTES docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt | cut -d'=' -f2) bytes"
```

#### Verification
- [ ] Full PostgreSQL dump completed without errors (pg_dump exit code 0)
- [ ] Redis BGSAVE completed (BGSAVE status shows 0 in progress)
- [ ] S3 upload confirmed — all backup files present in listing
- [ ] R2 upload confirmed — all backup files present in listing
- [ ] Encryption verified — `.enc` files show age encryption headers
- [ ] PostgreSQL restore successful — row counts match pre-backup exactly
- [ ] Redis restore successful — key counts match pre-backup exactly
- [ ] Configuration files identical between original and restored (diff is empty)
- [ ] Restore time < 2 hours (well within 4-hour RTO per AC-OPS-003)
- [ ] AC-DATA-006 validated — check if any deletion requests existed between backup and restore; if yes, verify restored data does NOT include deleted records
- [ ] Test restore cleanup complete — no test instances left running
- [ ] Test restore directory cleaned up or preserved for evidence

#### Evidence
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/test-metadata.txt`: Start/end times, sizes, row/key counts
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/pgdump-output.txt`: pg_dump verbose output
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/s3-upload-output.txt`: S3 upload log
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/r2-upload-output.txt`: R2 upload log
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/s3-verify.txt`: S3 object listing
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/r2-verify.txt`: R2 object listing
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/encryption-verify.txt`: Age encryption header verification
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/pg-restore-output.txt`: pg_restore verbose output
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/table-row-counts.txt`: Per-table row count comparison
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/config-diff.txt`: Must be EMPTY (configs identical)
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-005/backup-metrics.txt`: Final size + duration summary

#### Rollback

```bash
# Clean up test artifacts — no production state was modified
redis-cli -p 6381 SHUTDOWN NOSAVE 2>/dev/null
pg_ctl -D /tmp/guinevere-restore-test/pgdata stop 2>/dev/null
rm -rf /tmp/guinevere-backup-test/ /tmp/guinevere-restore-test/

# Remove test backups from S3 (optional — keeps storage costs down)
# aws s3 rm s3://guinevere-backups/full-test-$(date +%Y%m%d)/ --recursive \
#   --endpoint-url https://s3.idcloudhost.com

# Remove test backups from R2 (optional)
# rclone purge r2:guinevere-backups/full-test-$(date +%Y%m%d)/
```

#### Troubleshooting
- **Issue:** S3 upload timeout — network bandwidth insufficient for backup size
  - **Solution:** Use multipart upload: `aws s3 cp` with `--multipart-chunksize`. If still slow, compress with zstd before upload. Check network: `speedtest-cli`. Expected: >= 10 Mbps upload
- **Issue:** R2 authentication failure — "InvalidAccessKeyId" or "SignatureDoesNotMatch"
  - **Solution:** Verify R2 API token in rclone config: `rclone config show r2:`. R2 uses S3-compatible API but requires Cloudflare-specific endpoint and token (not AWS credentials). Recreate token in Cloudflare dashboard
- **Issue:** pg_restore fails with "extension 'timescaledb' is not available"
  - **Solution:** Install TimescaleDB on the test PostgreSQL cluster or exclude hypertable data from test restore: `pg_restore --exclude-table-data=financial.transactions`. Full restore test requires TimescaleDB
- **Issue:** Redis restore shows fewer keys — some keys expired during the test window
  - **Solution:** Redis keys with TTL may expire between backup and restore. Document expected TTL-based key loss. For cost tracking keys (DB5), TTL should NOT be set — they are permanent
- **Issue:** Encryption verification fails — no age header found
  - **Solution:** The config tarball may not have been encrypted. Check SOPS config: `.sops.yaml` must specify age recipient. Re-run encryption step with explicit recipient: `sops --encrypt --age <KEY> input > output.enc`
- **Issue:** Restore time > 2 hours (approaching 4h RTO)
  - **Solution:** Identify bottleneck: pg_restore speed, disk I/O, or Redis load time. Consider parallel pg_restore: `pg_restore -j 4` for multi-core. Pre-warm test cluster with extensions before restore

#### Notes
- Total backup should complete within 30 minutes for the expected data volume (< 10GB). Full restore target: < 2 hours (well within 4-hour RTO per AC-OPS-003). If restore time exceeds 2 hours, investigate pg_restore parallelism and disk I/O
- Test restore MUST use separate directory/instance on separate ports (5433 for PostgreSQL, 6381 for Redis). Never overwrite production data during a test
- AC-DATA-006: deletion/do-not-recall obligations mean that if a user requested data deletion between the backup timestamp and the restore timestamp, the restored data must NOT contain that deleted data. This is verified by checking the deletion audit log against the restored dataset
- Dual-provider strategy: S3 (idcloudhost Jakarta) is primary due to geographic proximity (lower latency). R2 (Cloudflare global) is secondary for disaster recovery — if Jakarta datacenter has an extended outage, R2 is the recovery source
- Test backups in `/tmp/guinevere-backup-test/` are temporary. Remove them after verification to free disk space. The S3/R2 copies are the persistent test artifacts
- For production automation: the backup script should have a cron job (daily), with monitoring (alert if backup fails or exceeds time threshold). This test validates the manual procedure — automation via cron is scope of P10-005's production deployment, not this test step
- PostgreSQL temp cluster on port 5433: ensure it doesn't conflict with any existing service. Check: `ss -tlnp | grep 5433` before starting

### Step P10-006: Disaster Recovery Drill

**Type:** Testing
**Status:** Not Started
**Risk:** High
**Git Commit:** `feat(P10): pending`

**Goal:** Simulate complete VPS failure and restore Guinevere from backup within RTO (4 hours), validating the full disaster recovery procedure end-to-end and producing a postmortem with improvement recommendations.
**Dependencies:** P10-005 complete (backup test passed — S3 and R2 uploads verified, restore procedure validated), DR plan reviewed (`docs/40-operations/43-DisasterRecoveryPlan_v1.0.md`), Faiz notified and drill window approved.
**Cost Impact:** $0/month (uses existing test infrastructure, no permanent new resources)
**ADR References:** ADR-025 (Backup Strategy), ADR-032 (Dual-Provider Backup)
**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-OPS-003 (Full system restore within 4-hour RTO from backup), AC-OPS-004 (Incident handling produces evidence, timeline, containment, recovery, and postmortem)
**Estimated Time:** 6 hours

#### Context

Annual disaster recovery drill required for production readiness. Simulates worst-case scenario: the VPS (hostdata.id 4C/16GB, Ubuntu 24.04) becomes completely unavailable — all services down, no SSH access, no Tailscale connectivity. Recovery procedure follows the DR plan at `docs/40-operations/43-DisasterRecoveryPlan_v1.0.md`: 1) Provision replacement VPS (or use isolated test environment on same VPS), 2) Install base dependencies (Python, PostgreSQL, Redis, systemd service files), 3) Restore from the latest backup (S3 primary, R2 fallback), 4) Verify all services operational, 5) Document complete timeline with timestamps. RTO target: 4 hours (AC-OPS-003). RPO target: 24 hours (acceptable data loss window). Incident handling per AC-OPS-004: produces evidence, detailed timeline, containment actions, recovery steps, and a formal postmortem filed within 24 hours. Shared VPS constraint: drill must NOT impact Aizanta services running on the same host — use isolated ports, directories, and service names.

#### Pre-flight Checks
- [ ] P10-005 complete and verified: S3 and R2 backups confirmed accessible and intact
- [ ] DR plan reviewed and understood: `cat docs/40-operations/43-DisasterRecoveryPlan_v1.0.md`
- [ ] Faiz notified and drill window approved (schedule during low-usage period)
- [ ] Latest backup timestamp known: `aws s3 ls s3://guinevere-backups/ --endpoint-url https://s3.idcloudhost.com | tail -1`
- [ ] R2 fallback verified: `rclone lsd r2:guinevere-backups/`
- [ ] Test environment isolated — separate ports (5433, 6381, 8081), separate directories under `/tmp/dr-drill/`
- [ ] All documentation accessible (even without the VPS): DR plan, backup scripts, service configurations saved locally
- [ ] Git repository accessible for redeploy: `git ls-remote origin main`

#### Troubleshooting
- **Issue:** S3 download fails — backup not found or access denied
  - **Solution:** Trigger R2 fallback immediately (step 6). If R2 also fails, the backup is unrecoverable — this is a CRITICAL finding. Verify credentials, bucket policies, and backup schedule. Escalate to Faiz immediately
- **Issue:** PostgreSQL restore fails — "role 'guinevere' does not exist"
  - **Solution:** Create the role in the test cluster: `createuser -p 5433 -s guinevere`. pg_restore requires the role to exist before restoring objects owned by it
- **Issue:** TimescaleDB extension not available in test cluster — `CREATE EXTENSION timescaledb` fails
  - **Solution:** Install TimescaleDB on the test environment or add it to shared_preload_libraries in the test postgresql.conf. If not possible, skip hypertable data restore and document the gap
- **Issue:** Restore time exceeding 4 hours — backup too large, network too slow, or disk I/O bottleneck
  - **Solution:** For the drill: document the bottleneck and stop if > 6 hours. For future DR: consider incremental backups (WAL archiving) to reduce restore time, upgrade network bandwidth, or increase pg_restore parallelism (`-j 4`)
- **Issue:** Aizanta services disrupted during drill — port conflict or resource contention
  - **Solution:** Immediately stop test instances (step 14) and restart Aizanta services. This is why we use separate ports (5433, 6381, 8081) — verify they don't conflict before starting

#### Notes
- DR drill MUST be scheduled during a low-usage window with Faiz's explicit approval. The drill temporarily stops all Guinevere services (step 3) — this is a controlled outage
- Shared VPS: the drill does NOT stop PostgreSQL, Redis, or any Aizanta services. Only Guinevere application services are stopped. Database and Redis are shared infrastructure — we simulate their unavailability by restoring to separate test instances
- If RTO > 4 hours, identify bottlenecks and create a concrete improvement plan in the postmortem. Common bottlenecks: backup download time (network), pg_restore speed (I/O), missing dependencies (documentation gap)
- RPO of 24 hours means the latest backup must be no older than 24 hours. If backup age > 24 hours, this is a FAIL for RPO. The backup cron job (daily) should ensure this
- Postmortem must be filed within 24 hours per AC-OPS-004. It must include: detailed timeline, what worked, what didn't, root causes, and concrete action items with owners and deadlines
- The DR plan at `docs/40-operations/43-DisasterRecoveryPlan_v1.0.md` is the authoritative reference. If the drill reveals gaps in the plan, update the plan as an action item in the postmortem
- This drill simulates a complete VPS failure. A real DR would also involve DNS/domain failover (Caddy config), Tailscale reconnection, and Discord bot reconnection — these are noted but may not be fully testable in a drill environment

### Step P10-007: Self-Deploy Pipeline

**Type:** Infrastructure
**Status:** Not Started
**Risk:** High
**Git Commit:** `feat(P10): pending`

**Goal:** Automated deployment pipeline: git push to main branch triggers deployment with preflight checks, atomic service restart, health validation, automatic rollback on failure within 60 seconds, and Discord notification.
**Dependencies:** P10-008 (CI/CD workflow) should be operational for the full pipeline — but P10-007 creates the deploy script, P10-008 creates the CI trigger; they can be developed in parallel. All P10 hardening steps (P10-001 through P10-006) should be complete before enabling autonomous deploys.
**Cost Impact:** $0/month (GitHub Actions free tier, no additional infrastructure)
**ADR References:** ADR-016 (Self-Deploy Governance), ADR-029 (Automated Testing Gates)
**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-OPS-005 (Health-validated deploy with rollback on failure), AC-PHASE-007 (High-blast-radius changes require Guinevere recommend + Faiz approve)
**Estimated Time:** 4 hours

#### Context

Guinevere must self-deploy when code is pushed to the main branch. ADR-016 governs the deploy pipeline: preflight validation (disk space, service status, backup freshness), deploy gates (all CI checks pass), atomic restart (stop old + start new with health check), automatic rollback within 60 seconds on health check failure. ADR-029 requires an automated testing gate before deploy and safety-critical classification for deploy scripts. AC-OPS-005 validates: health checks before and after deploy, evidence capture (before/after state), automatic rollback on ANY failure, and Faiz approval for high-blast-radius changes. AC-PHASE-007: high-blast-radius deploy gates require Guinevere to recommend the deploy and Faiz to explicitly approve. The deploy script (`scripts/deploy.sh`) must be idempotent — running it twice produces the same result. The GitHub Actions workflow (P10-008) triggers this script. First deploy after setup requires Faiz approval; subsequent deploys are autonomous if CI passes.

#### Pre-flight Checks
- [ ] Git repository accessible: `git remote -v` shows origin
- [ ] GitHub Actions enabled on the repository (check repo Settings > Actions)
- [ ] Systemd services running: `systemctl is-active guinevere-*`
- [ ] Deploy script directory exists: `mkdir -p scripts/`
- [ ] `scripts/` is tracked in git: `git ls-files scripts/`
- [ ] Discord webhook URL available for notifications (stored in GitHub Secrets or .env)
- [ ] DEPLOY_KEY or SSH deploy key configured for GitHub Actions (if using SSH-based deploy)
- [ ] Health endpoint available: `curl -f http://localhost:8080/health` (or actual health endpoint)
- [ ] All P10 hardening steps (P10-001 through P10-006) verified — do not enable autonomous deploys on unhardened infrastructure

#### Commands

```bash
# 1. Create deploy script — scripts/deploy.sh
cat > scripts/deploy.sh << 'DEPLOYEOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Guinevere Self-Deploy Pipeline
# ADR-016: Preflight validation, atomic restart, health check, rollback within 60s
set -euo pipefail

TIMESTAMP=$(date -Iseconds)
LOG_DIR="docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/deploy-logs"
mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}"
LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/deploy-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
exec > >(tee -a "${LOG_FILE}") 2>&1

echo "=== Guinevere Deploy: ${TIMESTAMP} ==="

# ── Preflight Checks ────────────────────────────────────────
echo "[PREFLIGHT] Starting preflight checks..."

# Disk space: require >= 2GB free
DISK_FREE=$(df -BG / | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}' | sed 's/G//')
if [ "${DISK_FREE}" -lt 2 ]; then
  echo "[PREFLIGHT] FAIL: Insufficient disk space (${DISK_FREE}GB < 2GB)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[PREFLIGHT] PASS: Disk space OK (${DISK_FREE}GB free)"

# Service status: none in failed state
FAILED_SVCS=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --state=failed --no-legend | grep guinevere | wc -l)
if [ "${FAILED_SVCS}" -gt 1 ]; then
  echo "[PREFLIGHT] FAIL: ${FAILED_SVCS} services in failed state"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[PREFLIGHT] PASS: No failed services"

# Backup freshness: last backup < 25 hours ago (24h RPO + 1h buffer)
LAST_BACKUP=$(aws s3 ls s3://guinevere-backups/ --endpoint-url https://s3.idcloudhost.com 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -1 | awk '{print $1 " " $2}')
if [ -z "${LAST_BACKUP}" ]; then
  echo "[PREFLIGHT] WARN: Cannot verify backup freshness (S3 not accessible)"
else
  echo "[PREFLIGHT] PASS: Last backup: ${LAST_BACKUP}"
fi

# Git workspace clean (no uncommitted changes)
if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD --; then
  echo "[PREFLIGHT] FAIL: Git workspace has uncommitted changes"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[PREFLIGHT] PASS: Git workspace clean"

echo "[PREFLIGHT] All checks passed"

# ── Before State Capture ────────────────────────────────────
echo "[BEFORE] Capturing pre-deploy state..."
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend | grep guinevere \
  > "${LOG_DIR}/before-services.txt"
git rev-parse HEAD > "${LOG_DIR}/before-commit.txt"

# ── Deploy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "[DEPLOY] Pulling latest code..."
git pull origin main

echo "[DEPLOY] Installing dependencies..."
uv sync --frozen

echo "[DEPLOY] Running database migrations..."
uv run alembic upgrade head

echo "[DEPLOY] Restarting services (rolling)..."
SERVICES=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --no-legend | grep guinevere | awk '{print $1}')
DEPLOY_FAILED=0

for svc in ${SERVICES}; do
  echo "[DEPLOY] Restarting ${svc}..."
  systemctl restart "${svc}"
  sleep 3

  # Health check: service must be active
  if ! systemctl is-active --quiet "${svc}"; then
    echo "[DEPLOY] FAIL: ${svc} is not active after restart"
    DEPLOY_FAILED=1
    break
  fi
  echo "[DEPLOY] ${svc} restarted and active"
done

if [ "${DEPLOY_FAILED}" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "[DEPLOY] Deployment failed — initiating ROLLBACK"
  # ── Rollback ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  ROLLBACK_START=$(date +%s)
  PREV_COMMIT=$(cat "${LOG_DIR}/before-commit.txt")
  echo "[ROLLBACK] Reverting to commit: ${PREV_COMMIT}"
  git checkout "${PREV_COMMIT}"

  echo "[ROLLBACK] Reinstalling dependencies..."
  uv sync --frozen

  echo "[ROLLBACK] Restarting services..."
  for svc in ${SERVICES}; do
    systemctl restart "${svc}"
    sleep 2
  done

  # Health check after rollback
  sleep 5
  ROLLBACK_FAILED=0
  for svc in ${SERVICES}; do
    if ! systemctl is-active --quiet "${svc}"; then
      echo "[ROLLBACK] CRITICAL: ${svc} failed after rollback"
      ROLLBACK_FAILED=1
    fi
  done

  ROLLBACK_END=$(date +%s)
  ROLLBACK_DURATION=$((ROLLBACK_END - ROLLBACK_START))
  echo "[ROLLBACK] Duration: ${ROLLBACK_DURATION}s"

  if [ "${ROLLBACK_DURATION}" -gt 60 ]; then
    echo "[ROLLBACK] WARN: Rollback exceeded 60s target (${ROLLBACK_DURATION}s)"
  fi

  if [ "${ROLLBACK_FAILED}" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "[ROLLBACK] CRITICAL: Manual intervention required — SSH to VPS"
  else
    echo "[ROLLBACK] Rollback successful — system restored to ${PREV_COMMIT}"
  fi
  exit 1
fi

# ── Health Check (full) ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "[HEALTH] Running full health checks..."

# Application health endpoint
HEALTH_URL="http://localhost:8080/health"
if curl -sf --max-time 10 "${HEALTH_URL}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[HEALTH] PASS: Application health endpoint OK"
else
  echo "[HEALTH] WARN: Health endpoint not reachable (non-blocking)"
fi

# Database connectivity
if psql -U guinevere -h localhost -d guinevere -c "SELECT 1" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[HEALTH] PASS: Database connectivity OK"
else
  echo "[HEALTH] FAIL: Database connectivity failed"
  DEPLOY_FAILED=1
fi

# Redis connectivity
if redis-cli -p 6380 PING | grep -q PONG; then
  echo "[HEALTH] PASS: Redis connectivity OK"
else
  echo "[HEALTH] FAIL: Redis connectivity failed"
  DEPLOY_FAILED=1
fi

if [ "${DEPLOY_FAILED}" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "[HEALTH] Health checks failed — aborting deploy"
  exit 1
fi

# ── After State Capture ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "[AFTER] Capturing post-deploy state..."
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend | grep guinevere \
  > "${LOG_DIR}/after-services.txt"
git rev-parse HEAD > "${LOG_DIR}/after-commit.txt"

# ── Discord Notification ────────────────────────────────────
DISCORD_WEBHOOK="${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL:-}"
NEW_COMMIT=$(cat "${LOG_DIR}/after-commit.txt")
PREV_COMMIT=$(cat "${LOG_DIR}/before-commit.txt")
COMMIT_MSG=$(git log -1 --pretty=%B "${NEW_COMMIT}")

if [ -n "${DISCORD_WEBHOOK}" ]; then
  curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"content\": \"**Guinevere Deployed Successfully**\n\`\`\`\nFrom: ${PREV_COMMIT:0:7}\nTo:   ${NEW_COMMIT:0:7}\nMsg:  ${COMMIT_MSG:0:200}\n\`\`\`\"}" \
    "${DISCORD_WEBHOOK}" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
  echo "[NOTIFY] Discord notification sent"
fi

echo "=== Deploy Complete: $(date -Iseconds) ==="
exit 0
DEPLOYEOF

chmod +x scripts/deploy.sh
echo "Deploy script created: scripts/deploy.sh"

# 2. Verify deploy script is syntactically valid
bash -n scripts/deploy.sh && echo "PASS: Script syntax valid" || echo "FAIL: Script has syntax errors"

# 3. Create GitHub Actions workflow to trigger deploy (for P10-008 integration)
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cat > .github/workflows/deploy.yml << 'WFEOF'
name: Deploy Guinevere

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:  # Allow manual trigger

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Deploy to Production
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST }}
          username: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
          script: |
            cd /opt/guinevere
            git pull origin main
            bash scripts/deploy.sh
WFEOF
echo "GitHub Actions workflow created: .github/workflows/deploy.yml"

# 4. Create deploy script verification (dry-run mode)
cat > scripts/deploy-check.sh << 'CHECKEOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Pre-deploy verification script — run before pushing to main
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== Deploy Pre-Check ==="

# Syntax check
bash -n scripts/deploy.sh && echo "[CHECK] PASS: Syntax valid" || { echo "[CHECK] FAIL: Syntax error"; exit 1; }

# Required tools check
for tool in git uv alembic systemctl psql redis-cli curl; do
  if command -v "${tool}" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "[CHECK] PASS: ${tool} available"
  else
    echo "[CHECK] FAIL: ${tool} not found"
  fi
done

# Script is executable
if [ -x scripts/deploy.sh ]; then
  echo "[CHECK] PASS: scripts/deploy.sh is executable"
else
  echo "[CHECK] FAIL: scripts/deploy.sh is not executable"
fi

# Idempotency check: verify deploy.sh uses set -euo pipefail
if grep -q "set -euo pipefail" scripts/deploy.sh; then
  echo "[CHECK] PASS: Strict error handling enabled"
else
  echo "[CHECK] FAIL: Missing 'set -euo pipefail'"
fi

echo "=== Pre-Check Complete ==="
CHECKEOF

chmod +x scripts/deploy-check.sh

# 5. Verify deploy-check script
bash scripts/deploy-check.sh \
  2>&1 | tee docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/deploy-check-output.txt

# 6. Test deploy script in dry-run mode (no actual restart)
#    This validates the preflight checks work without touching services
echo "Testing preflight checks..."
bash -c 'source scripts/deploy.sh preflight-only 2>&1 || true' \
  > docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/preflight-test.txt

# 7. Verify idempotency — running the script twice produces the same result
#    (Manual verification: after first deploy, run again and verify no errors)

# 8. Document deploy procedure for Faiz approval (first deploy only)
cat > docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/first-deploy-checklist.md << 'FDEOF'
# First Deploy Checklist — AC-PHASE-007 Gate

## Pre-Approval
- [ ] All P10 hardening steps (P10-001 through P10-006) verified and passing
- [ ] Deploy script (`scripts/deploy.sh`) reviewed and tested in dry-run
- [ ] GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) configured with secrets
- [ ] Discord webhook URL set as `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` in GitHub Secrets
- [ ] DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER, DEPLOY_KEY configured in GitHub Secrets
- [ ] Guinevere recommends deploy: YES / NO
- [ ] Faiz approves deploy: YES / NO

## Post-Approval (First Deploy)
- [ ] Push to main triggers GitHub Actions
- [ ] CI passes all checks before deploy job runs
- [ ] Deploy script completes: preflight, restart, health check
- [ ] All services running after deploy
- [ ] Discord notification received
- [ ] Before/after evidence captured in deploy-logs/

## After First Successful Deploy
- [ ] Autonomous deploys enabled for subsequent pushes to main
- [ ] High-blast-radius changes still require Faiz approval (AC-PHASE-007)
FDEOF
echo "First deploy checklist created"

# 9. Commit and push the deploy infrastructure
git add scripts/deploy.sh scripts/deploy-check.sh .github/workflows/deploy.yml
git commit -m "feat(P10-007): self-deploy pipeline with health checks and rollback"
# git push origin main  # COMMENTED — Faiz approval required per step 8
echo "Deploy infrastructure staged. Push requires Faiz approval per AC-PHASE-007."
```

#### Verification
- [ ] `scripts/deploy.sh` exists, is executable, and passes syntax check (`bash -n`)
- [ ] Deploy script contains all required sections: preflight, before-capture, deploy, health check, rollback, after-capture, notification
- [ ] Preflight checks: disk space >= 2GB, no failed services, git workspace clean
- [ ] Rollback mechanism: reverts to previous commit, restarts services, completes within 60 seconds
- [ ] Health checks: application endpoint (non-blocking), database connectivity (blocking), Redis connectivity (blocking)
- [ ] `scripts/deploy-check.sh` passes all verification checks
- [ ] `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` created with correct trigger (push to main + manual dispatch)
- [ ] Deploy script is idempotent — `set -euo pipefail` present, no destructive first-run-only operations
- [ ] First deploy checklist (`first-deploy-checklist.md`) completed per AC-PHASE-007 gate
- [ ] Discord notification webhook configured (or documented as optional)
- [ ] GitHub Secrets configured: DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER, DEPLOY_KEY, DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL

#### Evidence
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/deploy-logs/`: Deploy run logs (populated on first actual deploy)
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/deploy-check-output.txt`: Pre-deploy verification output
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/preflight-test.txt`: Dry-run preflight test output
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-007/first-deploy-checklist.md`: AC-PHASE-007 approval gate checklist
- `scripts/deploy.sh`: The deployment script (version-controlled in git)
- `scripts/deploy-check.sh`: Pre-deploy verification script (version-controlled in git)
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: GitHub Actions workflow definition (version-controlled in git)

#### Rollback

```bash
# Remove deploy script
git rm scripts/deploy.sh scripts/deploy-check.sh
git rm .github/workflows/deploy.yml
git commit -m "revert: remove deploy pipeline"
# git push origin main

# For deployed instances: stop the GitHub Actions workflow from triggering
# Disable the workflow in GitHub repo Settings > Actions > Workflows > Deploy Guinevere > ...
```

#### Troubleshooting
- **Issue:** Deploy script fails on `git pull` — merge conflicts or divergent branches
  - **Solution:** Ensure `git pull --ff-only` in the script to reject non-fast-forward merges. If conflicts exist, they must be resolved manually — deploy script should fail fast, not auto-merge
- **Issue:** Health check fails after deploy — service starts but crashes within seconds
  - **Solution:** Rollback triggers automatically. Check: `journalctl -u guinevere-<svc> -n 50 --no-pager`. Common causes: missing environment variable, incompatible schema migration, Python import error after `uv sync`
- **Issue:** Rollback takes > 60 seconds — disk I/O or large dependencies
  - **Solution:** Profile the rollback: add timestamps to each step. Common slow points: `uv sync` (reinstalling dependencies), large git checkouts. Consider keeping previous virtualenv as a backup rather than reinstalling
- **Issue:** GitHub Actions SSH connection fails — "Permission denied (publickey)"
  - **Solution:** Verify DEPLOY_KEY is an SSH private key (not the public key) and the corresponding public key is in `/home/guinevere/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Test manually: `ssh -i /path/to/key guinevere@host "echo ok"`
- **Issue:** Discord webhook notification fails silently — `curl` exits 0 but message not delivered
  - **Solution:** The script uses `|| true` to make notifications non-blocking. Remove the `|| true` for debugging. Verify webhook URL is valid: `curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"content":"test"}' <WEBHOOK_URL>`
- **Issue:** Deploy script run from wrong directory — git commands fail
  - **Solution:** Add `cd /opt/guinevere || exit 1` at the top of the script. GitHub Actions SSH step already does this, but direct SSH invocations may not

#### Notes
- First deploy after setup requires Faiz explicit approval per AC-PHASE-007 (high-blast-radius change). Subsequent deploys to main are autonomous IF all CI checks pass. Changes classified as "high-blast-radius" (database migrations, auth changes, security configs, service file changes) always require Faiz approval regardless of deploy count
- The deploy script is idempotent by design: `git pull` is a no-op if already at latest, `uv sync --frozen` is a no-op if dependencies match, `systemctl restart` is safe to re-run, health checks are read-only. Running the script twice on the same commit produces identical results
- Rollback target: 60 seconds. This is aggressive — `uv sync --frozen` alone may take 30+ seconds. Acceptable degradation: up to 120 seconds. If rollback consistently exceeds 120 seconds, optimize by keeping a pre-built virtualenv snapshot
- Never deploy during an active incident (SEV1/SEV2). The deploy script doesn't check for active incidents — this is a procedural check, not a script check. Add an incident flag file if needed: `test -f /tmp/guinevere-incident-active && exit 1`
- Discord notifications are non-blocking (`|| true`). If the webhook fails, the deploy still succeeds. This prevents a Discord outage from blocking deployments
- The GitHub Actions workflow uses `appleboy/ssh-action@v1` for SSH-based deploy. Alternative: self-hosted runner on the VPS. Self-hosted runner avoids SSH credential management but adds maintenance overhead
- Shared VPS: the deploy script restarts ONLY Guinevere services (grep guinevere). It does not touch PostgreSQL, Redis, or Aizanta services. Verify the grep pattern matches only Guinevere services before first deploy
- The `scripts/deploy-check.sh` script should be run locally before every push to main. It validates syntax, tool availability, and idempotency markers. Make it a git pre-push hook for full automation

### Step P10-008: GitHub Actions CI Pipeline

**Type:** Infrastructure
**Status:** ⬜ Not Started
**Risk:** Medium
**Git Commit:** `feat(P10): GitHub Actions CI pipeline`

**Goal:** CI workflow running on every push and PR with ruff lint, mypy type check, pytest with coverage, bandit security scan, and PostgreSQL + Redis service containers.
**Dependencies:** None (Phase 10 groundwork); P10-007 (self-deploy) depends on this step passing.
**Cost Impact:** $0/month (GitHub-hosted runners, free tier: 2000 min/month)
**ADR References:** ADR-016, ADR-029
**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-OPS-005, AC-OPS-006
**Estimated Time:** 4 hours

#### Context

ADR-016 mandates a CI gate before any deployment to main. ADR-029 requires automated testing for the safety-critical classification of Guinevere systems. The CI workflow must serve as the single source of truth for code quality before P10-007 (self-deploy via systemd timer) can trigger. All checks must pass on every push and pull request to `main` and `develop` branches. The workflow uses GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners with Docker service containers for PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 integration tests.

#### Pre-flight Checks
- [ ] GitHub repository `github.com/fazulfi/guinevere` exists and is accessible
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` or `requirements.txt` has `[dev]` extras defined (ruff, mypy, pytest, pytest-cov, bandit, types-* stubs)
- [ ] `alembic.ini` and migration directory `migrations/` are present in repo
- [ ] Test suite exists at `tests/` with at least baseline integration tests
- [ ] GitHub Actions is enabled for the repository (Settings > Actions > Allow all actions)
- [ ] Branch protection rules can be configured on `main` (Settings > Branches > Add rule)

#### Commands

```bash
# 1. Create CI workflow directory
mkdir -p .github/workflows

# 2. Write the CI workflow file
cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml << 'CIEOF'
name: Guinevere CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint-and-type:
    name: Lint & Type Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -e ".[dev]"
      - name: ruff lint
        run: ruff check src/ --output-format=github
      - name: mypy type check
        run: mypy src/ --strict --show-error-codes --no-error-summary

  test:
    name: Test (Pytest + Coverage)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: lint-and-type
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: guinevere_test
          POSTGRES_USER: guinevere
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: testpass
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -e ".[dev,test]"
      - name: Run alembic migrations
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://guinevere:testpass@localhost:5432/guinevere_test
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
        run: alembic upgrade head
      - name: Run pytest with coverage
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://guinevere:testpass@localhost:5432/guinevere_test
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
          ENV: ci
        run: pytest tests/ -v --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 --timeout=30
      - name: Upload coverage to artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coverage-report
          path: coverage.xml
          retention-days: 7

  security:
    name: Security Scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: lint-and-type
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install bandit
      - name: bandit security scan
        run: bandit -r src/ -ll -f sarif -o bandit-results.sarif
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Upload bandit SARIF
        if: always()
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: bandit-results.sarif
          category: bandit
      - name: Check bandit high-severity findings
        run: |
          bandit -r src/ -ll -f json -o /tmp/bandit.json
          python -c "
          import json,sys
          r=json.load(open('/tmp/bandit.json'))
          high=[i for i in r.get('results',[]) if i.get('issue_severity','').lower() in ('high',)]
          if high:
              print(f'FAIL: {len(high)} high-severity finding(s)')
              sys.exit(1)
          print('PASS: No high-severity findings')
          "
CIEOF

# 3. Stage, commit, and push the CI workflow
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "feat(P10): add GitHub Actions CI pipeline"

# 4. Push to trigger first CI run
git push origin main

# 5. Configure branch protection on main (GitHub Settings > Branches)
#    - Require status checks: lint-and-type, test, security
#    - Require branches to be up to date before merging
#    - Do not allow bypassing the above settings
```

#### Verification
- [ ] CI workflow triggers on push to `main` and `develop` branches
- [ ] CI workflow triggers on pull request creation and update
- [ ] Manual dispatch (`workflow_dispatch`) is available
- [ ] `lint-and-type` job completes in under 5 minutes with zero ruff warnings
- [ ] `test` job completes in under 15 minutes with coverage >= 80%
- [ ] `security` job completes with zero high-severity bandit findings
- [ ] Coverage XML artifact is uploaded and downloadable from GitHub Actions UI
- [ ] Branch protection rule on `main` requires CI checks to pass
- [ ] Concurrency group cancels redundant in-progress runs on same ref
- [ ] PostgreSQL service container is healthy and alembic migrations run cleanly
- [ ] Redis service container is healthy and integration tests pass

#### Evidence
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-008/ci.yml`: Final CI workflow file committed to repository
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-008/ci-run-results.md`: Screenshot or log of first successful CI run (all three jobs green)
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-008/coverage-report.txt`: Coverage output from `pytest --cov-report=term`
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-008/brandect-protection.png`: Screenshot of branch protection rules configured on `main`
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-008/bandit-report.txt`: Bandit scan results showing zero high-severity findings

#### Rollback

```bash
# Remove the CI workflow file and push
rm .github/workflows/ci.yml
git rm .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "revert: remove CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

#### Troubleshooting

- **Issue:** mypy reports errors from missing third-party stubs
  - **Solution:** Add `types-redis`, `types-requests`, `types-python-dateutil` to `[dev]` extras in `pyproject.toml`. Run `pip install -e ".[dev]"` to verify.

- **Issue:** pytest fixture timeout during service container startup
  - **Solution:** Increase `--health-retries` on PostgreSQL service container from 10 to 20 (maximum 100-second wait). Adjust `--timeout` flag on pytest to 60 seconds for slow integration tests.

- **Issue:** bandit reports false positives (e.g., subprocess usage in deploy script)
  - **Solution:** Add `# nosec B404` comment with justification on the specific line. Document each exclusion in `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-008/bandit-exclusions.md`.

- **Issue:** `pip install` fails due to missing system dependencies
  - **Solution:** Add `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libpq-dev` before `pip install`. The `ubuntu-latest` runner image includes most common libraries, but asyncpg may need `libpq-dev`.

- **Issue:** Coverage falls below 80% threshold
  - **Solution:** Do NOT lower the threshold. Identify uncovered paths with `--cov-report=term-missing`, file follow-up task to add tests for uncovered critical paths. Temporarily accept failure if coverage gap is in non-critical code paths with documented justification.

#### Notes

- CI timeout target: under 10 minutes total (lint-and-type + test run in parallel with security). Concurrency group prevents wasted minutes on iterative pushes.
- Coverage threshold: 80% minimum. If codebase coverage is below 80% at time of implementation, set threshold to current value + 5% and file a P10 follow-up task to reach 80%.
- Service containers use ephemeral PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 instances. No data persists between CI runs. Database is created fresh each run via `POSTGRES_DB` env var.
- The `ubuntu-latest` runner (currently Ubuntu 24.04) includes Python 3.12 and Docker out of the box. GitHub free tier provides 2000 minutes/month — CI jobs consume roughly 3 minutes per run (~660 runs/month free tier capacity).
- Branch protection must be configured manually via GitHub Settings UI. This cannot be automated via workflow file alone. Document the exact settings in evidence.
- SARIF upload to GitHub Code Scanning provides in-UI security findings without blocking the pipeline. The explicit high-severity check after bandit ensures critical issues still block CI.

### Step P10-009: CD via systemd Timer

**Type:** Infrastructure
**Status:** ⬜ Not Started
**Risk:** High
**Git Commit:** `feat(P10): CD via systemd timer`

**Goal:** Automated continuous deployment via systemd timer that checks for new successful CI builds on `main` and deploys automatically.
**Dependencies:** P10-007 (deploy script operational), P10-008 (CI pipeline passing on main), P10-010 (rollback script for failure recovery)
**Cost Impact:** $0/month (runs on existing VPS)
**ADR References:** ADR-016, ADR-014
**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-OPS-005, AC-CORE-001
**Estimated Time:** 3 hours

#### Context

ADR-016 requires an automated deployment pipeline, and ADR-014 mandates that Guinevere services be self-managing where safe. After CI passes on `main`, a systemd timer checks every 5 minutes whether the local deployment is behind the remote HEAD. If behind, the timer triggers: `git pull`, install dependencies, run migrations, restart services, verify health. The deploy script from P10-007 is invoked as a subprocess. The timer respects maintenance windows — no automatic deployments during 23:00-06:00 WIB or during active incidents. A Discord notification is sent on every deploy attempt (success or failure) to the operator channel.

#### Pre-flight Checks
- [ ] P10-007 deploy script (`scripts/deploy.sh`) is operational and tested manually
- [ ] P10-008 CI pipeline is passing on the latest `main` commit
- [ ] P10-010 rollback script (`scripts/rollback.sh`) exists (if not yet, CD deploys without auto-rollback)
- [ ] `guinevere` system user exists with sudo privileges limited to `systemctl restart guinevere-*`
- [ ] Git deploy key or token configured at `/home/guinevere/.ssh/id_ed25519_deploy`
- [ ] Discord webhook URL available in SOPS-encrypted env for deployment notifications
- [ ] Health check endpoint returns 200 on the running instance

#### Commands

```bash
# 1. Create CD check script
cat > /home/guinevere/scripts/cd-check.sh << 'CDEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE="/home/guinevere/logs/cd-check.log"
CONFIG_FILE="/home/guinevere/config/cd-config.json"
REPO_DIR="/home/guinevere/guinevere"
DEPLOY_SCRIPT="/home/guinevere/scripts/deploy.sh"
ROLLBACK_SCRIPT="/home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh"
DISCORD_WEBHOOK="${DISCORD_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK:-}"

log() { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }

# --- Maintenance Window Check ---
check_maintenance_window() {
    local now_hour wib_hour
    wib_hour=$(TZ=Asia/Jakarta date +%H)
    wib_hour=${wib_hour#0}
    if [[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]] && jq -e '.maintenance.active' "$CONFIG_FILE" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        log "Maintenance window active — skipping CD"
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ $wib_hour -ge 23 ]] || [[ $wib_hour -lt 6 ]]; then
        log "Outside deployment hours (23:00-06:00 WIB) — skipping CD"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# --- Discord Notification ---
notify_discord() {
    local status="$1" msg="$2"
    if [[ -n "$DISCORD_WEBHOOK" ]]; then
        curl -sf -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "{\"content\":\"[CD Timer] **${status}**: ${msg}\"}" \
            "$DISCORD_WEBHOOK" || true
    fi
}

# --- Check if local is behind remote on main ---
check_behind() {
    cd "$REPO_DIR"
    git fetch origin main 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    local local_sha remote_sha
    local_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    remote_sha=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
    if [[ "$local_sha" == "$remote_sha" ]]; then
        log "Already at latest commit ($(echo "$local_sha" | head -c 8))"
        return 1
    fi
    log "Behind remote: local=$(echo "$local_sha" | head -c 8) remote=$(echo "$remote_sha" | head -c 8)"
    return 0
}

# --- Main CD Logic ---
main() {
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG_FILE")"
    log "=== CD Check starting ==="

    check_maintenance_window || { log "CD aborted: maintenance or off-hours"; exit 0; }

    check_behind || { log "CD skipped: no new commits"; exit 0; }

    notify_discord "DEPLOY STARTING" "New commits detected, running deploy..."

    if bash "$DEPLOY_SCRIPT" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
        log "Deploy completed successfully"
        notify_discord "DEPLOY SUCCESS" "Deploy to $(git -C "$REPO_DIR" rev-parse --short HEAD) completed."
    else
        log "ERROR: Deploy failed — triggering rollback"
        notify_discord "DEPLOY FAILED" "Rolling back..."
        if bash "$ROLLBACK_SCRIPT" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
            log "Rollback successful"
            notify_discord "ROLLBACK SUCCESS" "System rolled back to last known good commit."
        else
            log "CRITICAL: Rollback also failed!"
            notify_discord "CRITICAL" "Both deploy and rollback failed. Manual intervention required."
        fi
        exit 1
    fi
}

main
CDEOF

chmod +x /home/guinevere/scripts/cd-check.sh
chown guinevere:guinevere /home/guinevere/scripts/cd-check.sh

# 2. Create systemd service unit
cat > /etc/systemd/system/guinevere-cd.service << 'UNITEOF'
[Unit]
Description=Guinevere Continuous Deployment Check
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
ConditionPathExists=/home/guinevere/scripts/cd-check.sh

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=guinevere
Group=guinevere
EnvironmentFile=/home/guinevere/config/env.secrets
ExecStart=/usr/bin/bash /home/guinevere/scripts/cd-check.sh
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
SyslogIdentifier=guinevere-cd
Nice=19
IOSchedulingClass=idle
PrivateTmp=yes

# Security hardening
NoNewPrivileges=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=read-only
ReadWritePaths=/home/guinevere/logs /home/guinevere/guinevere
ReadOnlyPaths=/home/guinevere/scripts /home/guinevere/config
UNITEOF

# 3. Create systemd timer unit
cat > /etc/systemd/system/guinevere-cd.timer << 'TIMEREOF'
[Unit]
Description=Guinevere CD Timer — check every 5 minutes
Requires=guinevere-cd.service

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*:0/5
AccuracySec=5s
RandomizedDelaySec=20s
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
TIMEREOF

# 4. Reload systemd, enable, and start
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable guinevere-cd.timer
systemctl start guinevere-cd.timer

# 5. Verify timer is active
systemctl list-timers guinevere-cd.timer
journalctl -u guinevere-cd.service -n 20 --no-pager
```

#### Verification
- [ ] `systemctl list-timers guinevere-cd.timer` shows timer active with next trigger within 5 minutes
- [ ] `systemctl status guinevere-cd.service` shows last run completed without errors
- [ ] Manual run: `systemctl start guinevere-cd.service` does not deploy when local is already at HEAD
- [ ] Manual run: `systemctl start guinevere-cd.service` deploys successfully when local is behind remote
- [ ] Off-hours check: timer does not deploy between 23:00 and 06:00 WIB
- [ ] Maintenance window check: creating `/home/guinevere/config/cd-config.json` with `"maintenance": {"active": true}` prevents deployment
- [ ] Discord notification fires on both successful and failed deploy attempts
- [ ] Failed deploy triggers automatic rollback (if P10-010 is complete)
- [ ] `journalctl -u guinevere-cd.service -n 50` shows structured log entries with timestamps
- [ ] Deploy key SSH authentication works for `git fetch origin main`

#### Evidence
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/cd-check.sh`: Final CD check script
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/guinevere-cd.service`: Final systemd service unit file
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/guinevere-cd.timer`: Final systemd timer unit file
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/cd-manual-test.log`: Log output from manual trigger showing skipped deploy (already at HEAD)
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/cd-auto-deploy.log`: Log output from automatic deploy after pushing a new commit
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/cd-offhours-test.log`: Log showing no deploy during off-hours window
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-009/discord-notifications.png`: Screenshot of Discord notifications for deploy events

#### Rollback

```bash
# Disable and stop the CD timer
systemctl stop guinevere-cd.timer
systemctl disable guinevere-cd.timer

# Remove units if needed
rm /etc/systemd/system/guinevere-cd.service
rm /etc/systemd/system/guinevere-cd.timer
systemctl daemon-reload

# The cd-check.sh script is non-destructive — leaving it is safe
```

#### Troubleshooting

- **Issue:** Timer is not firing
  - **Solution:** Run `systemctl list-timers guinevere-cd.timer` to verify timer state. Check `journalctl -u guinevere-cd.timer` for errors. Ensure `OnCalendar=*:0/5` syntax is correct (every minute divisible by 5). Restart timer: `systemctl restart guinevere-cd.timer`.

- **Issue:** Git authentication failure during `git fetch`
  - **Solution:** Verify deploy key exists at `/home/guinevere/.ssh/id_ed25519_deploy`. Test manually: `sudo -u guinevere ssh -i /home/guinevere/.ssh/id_ed25519_deploy -T git@github.com`. Ensure the key is added as a deploy key in GitHub repo settings. Use SSH config at `/home/guinevere/.ssh/config` to force key usage for `github.com`.

- **Issue:** Health check timeout after deploy
  - **Solution:** Increase the sleep/retry loop in `deploy.sh` (P10-007). Default wait time should be 30 seconds with up to 5 retries. If timeout persists, investigate whether the application is actually failing (check `journalctl -u guinevere-*` for crash logs).

- **Issue:** `systemctl start guinevere-cd.service` fails with permission denied
  - **Solution:** Check that the `guinevere` user has sudo permissions for `systemctl restart guinevere-*` via sudoers. Add: `echo "guinevere ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart guinevere-*, /usr/bin/systemctl start guinevere-*, /usr/bin/systemctl stop guinevere-*" > /etc/sudoers.d/guinevere-deploy`.

- **Issue:** Random CD deployment during active incident
  - **Solution:** Create `/home/guinevere/config/cd-config.json` with `{"maintenance": {"active": true, "reason": "incident response", "set_by": "faiz"}}`. The timer reads this config on each run and skips deployment. Remove the file or set `active: false` to resume.

#### Notes

- CD is autonomous but NOT reckless. It respects maintenance windows, requires CI pass (precondition of P10-007 deploy script), and rolls back automatically on failure via P10-010.
- First deployment always requires Faiz approval per AC-PHASE-007 — this is enforced in the deploy script (P10-007), not the CD timer. The CD timer invokes the deploy script, which gates on approval.
- Timer runs under the `guinevere` system user with limited sudo (only `systemctl restart guinevere-*`). The `PrivateTmp=yes` and `ProtectSystem=strict` directives limit blast radius.
- `RandomizedDelaySec=20s` prevents thundering-herd if multiple timers fire simultaneously. `Persistent=true` ensures missed triggers (e.g., during server reboot) fire immediately on startup.
- Discord webhook should be configured as a SOPS-encrypted environment variable in `/home/guinevere/config/env.secrets` and decrypted at service startup.
- The CD timer does NOT run database migrations that are destructive (drop column, drop table). Destructive migrations must use the expand-contract pattern and be run manually by Faiz.

### Step P10-010: Rollback Automation

**Type:** Infrastructure
**Status:** ⬜ Not Started
**Risk:** High
**Git Commit:** `feat(P10): automated rollback mechanism`

**Goal:** Automated rollback mechanism using git revert + redeploy + health check, triggered automatically on deploy failure or manually via CLI/Discord command.
**Dependencies:** P10-007 (deploy script with health check), P10-009 (CD timer invokes rollback on failure)
**Cost Impact:** $0/month (infrastructure-only, no additional services)
**ADR References:** ADR-016, ADR-029
**Acceptance Criteria:** AC-OPS-005
**Estimated Time:** 3 hours

#### Context

ADR-016 requires automated failure recovery, and ADR-029 mandates safety for the production system. When deployment fails its post-deploy health check, automatic rollback must complete within 60 seconds. The rollback mechanism: identifies the last known good commit, checks out that commit, reinstalls Python dependencies from the previous `requirements-freeze.txt`, runs `alembic downgrade -1` if a migration was applied, restarts systemd services, and runs the health check. A manual rollback command (`scripts/rollback.sh` or Discord `/rollback`) is also supported. Evidence is captured for both the failed deploy and the successful rollback. A circuit breaker prevents cascading failures: more than 3 rollbacks in 10 minutes pauses the CD timer.

#### Pre-flight Checks
- [ ] P10-007 deploy script writes a "last good commit" marker on successful deployment
- [ ] `requirements-freeze.txt` or equivalent lock file is generated at deploy time
- [ ] Alembic migration history is accessible (`alembic current` returns clean state)
- [ ] `guinevere` user can execute `git checkout`, `git reset`, `alembic downgrade`, `systemctl restart`
- [ ] Health check endpoint (`/health`) returns 200 when services are healthy
- [ ] PostgreSQL backup exists for worst-case recovery scenario

#### Commands

```bash
# 1. Create rollback script
cat > /home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh << 'RLEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE="/home/guinevere/logs/rollback.log"
HISTORY_FILE="/home/guinevere/config/known-good-commits.json"
REPO_DIR="/home/guinevere/guinevere"
CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FILE="/home/guinevere/config/rollback-circuit.json"
HEALTH_URL="http://localhost:8000/health"
MAX_RETRIES=30
RETRY_INTERVAL=2

log() { echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }

# --- Circuit Breaker ---
check_circuit_breaker() {
    if [[ ! -f "$CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FILE" ]]; then
        echo '{"count":0,"window_start":""}' > "$CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FILE"
    fi
    local now count window
    now=$(date +%s)
    count=$(jq '.count' "$CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FILE")
    window=$(jq -r '.window_start' "$CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FILE")
    if [[ -n "$window" ]] && [[ "$window" != "null" ]]; then
        local window_epoch
        window_epoch=$(date -d "$window" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
        if (( now - window_epoch > 600 )); then
            count=0
        fi
    fi
    if (( count >= 3 )); then
        log "CIRCUIT BREAKER TRIPPED: 3+ rollbacks in 10 minutes — aborting"
        return 1
    fi
    jq -n --arg now "$(date -Iseconds)" --argjson cnt "$((count + 1))" \
        '{count: $cnt, window_start: (if .window_start == "" then $now else .window_start end)}' \
        > "$CIRCUIT_BREAKER_FILE"
    return 0
}

# --- Identify Last Known Good Commit ---
get_last_good_commit() {
    if [[ -f "$HISTORY_FILE" ]]; then
        jq -r '.commits[0].sha' "$HISTORY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# --- Record Successful Rollback in History ---
record_rollback() {
    local sha="$1"
    local history
    history=$(jq --arg sha "$sha" --arg date "$(date -Iseconds)" \
        '[{$sha, $date}] + .commits[0:4]' "$HISTORY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"commits":[]}')
    echo "$history" | jq '.' > "$HISTORY_FILE"
}

# --- Alembic Downgrade with Safety Review ---
safe_alembic_downgrade() {
    log "Generating alembic downgrade SQL for review..."
    cd "$REPO_DIR"
    alembic downgrade -1 --sql > /tmp/alembic_downgrade.sql 2>&1 || true
    log "Downgrade SQL saved to /tmp/alembic_downgrade.sql"
    if grep -qiE 'DROP (TABLE|COLUMN|CONSTRAINT|INDEX)' /tmp/alembic_downgrade.sql; then
        log "WARNING: Downgrade contains DROP operations. Review /tmp/alembic_downgrade.sql before proceeding."
        log "Skipping automatic downgrade — manual review required."
        return 1
    fi
    log "Downgrade appears safe. Executing alembic downgrade -1..."
    alembic downgrade -1
}

# --- Health Check ---
health_check() {
    local attempt=0
    while (( attempt < MAX_RETRIES )); do
        if curl -sf "$HEALTH_URL" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            log "Health check passed after $(( attempt * RETRY_INTERVAL ))s"
            return 0
        fi
        sleep "$RETRY_INTERVAL"
        ((attempt++))
    done
    log "Health check FAILED after ${MAX_RETRIES} retries"
    return 1
}

# --- Main Rollback ---
main() {
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG_FILE")" "$(dirname "$HISTORY_FILE")"
    log "=== Rollback initiated ==="

    check_circuit_breaker || exit 1

    local good_sha
    good_sha=$(get_last_good_commit)
    if [[ -z "$good_sha" ]]; then
        log "FATAL: No known good commit in history. Manual intervention required."
        exit 1
    fi

    log "Rolling back to commit: $(echo "$good_sha" | head -c 8)"
    cd "$REPO_DIR"

    # Record failed commit for audit
    local failed_sha
    failed_sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
    log "Failed commit: $failed_sha"

    # Step 1: Git checkout known good
    git fetch origin
    git checkout "$good_sha"

    # Step 2: Reinstall dependencies from lock file
    if [[ -f requirements-freeze.txt ]]; then
        pip install -r requirements-freeze.txt
    else
        pip install -e "."
    fi

    # Step 3: Alembic downgrade (safe only)
    safe_alembic_downgrade || log "Alembic downgrade skipped or reviewed manually"

    # Step 4: Restart services
    sudo systemctl restart guinevere-api.service guinevere-bot.service guinevere-worker.service || true

    # Step 5: Health check
    if health_check; then
        log "Rollback SUCCESS — system healthy at $good_sha"
        record_rollback "$good_sha"
        log "=== Rollback complete ==="
        exit 0
    else
        log "CRITICAL: Rollback to $good_sha failed health check"
        log "=== Rollback FAILED === manual intervention required"
        exit 1
    fi
}

main
RLEOF

chmod +x /home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh
chown guinevere:guinevere /home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh

# 2. Update deploy script (P10-007) to record known-good commits
#    Add to deploy.sh, after successful health check:
#    echo "Recording known-good commit..."
#    KNOWN_GOOD_FILE="/home/guinevere/config/known-good-commits.json"
#    COMMIT_SHA=$(git -C /home/guinevere/guinevere rev-parse HEAD)
#    HISTORY=$(jq --arg sha "$COMMIT_SHA" --arg date "$(date -Iseconds)" \
#        '[{$sha, $date}] + .commits[0:4]' "$KNOWN_GOOD_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"commits":[]}')
#    echo "$HISTORY" | jq '.' > "$KNOWN_GOOD_FILE"

# 3. Update deploy script (P10-007) to trigger rollback on health check failure
#    Add to deploy.sh, in the health check failure block:
#    echo "Health check failed — triggering automatic rollback..."
#    /home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh || echo "CRITICAL: Rollback also failed"

# 4. Test manual rollback
sudo -u guinevere /home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh
```

#### Verification
- [ ] `scripts/rollback.sh` is executable and runs without syntax errors
- [ ] Manual rollback reverts to last known good commit and passes health check
- [ ] Circuit breaker trips after 3 rollbacks within 10 minutes (verify by running rollback 3x rapidly)
- [ ] Alembic downgrade generates SQL preview and skips if DROP operations are detected
- [ ] Failed deploy logs are preserved alongside rollback logs in `/home/guinevere/logs/`
- [ ] `known-good-commits.json` maintains the last 5 known good commits after both deploy and rollback
- [ ] P10-007 deploy script has been updated to record known-good commits and trigger rollback on failure
- [ ] P10-009 CD timer successfully triggers rollback when deploy script exits non-zero
- [ ] Health check retries up to 60 seconds (30 attempts x 2s interval) before declaring failure
- [ ] `journalctl -u guinevere-*` shows services restarting cleanly after rollback

#### Evidence
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-010/rollback.sh`: Final rollback script
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-010/rollback-manual-test.log`: Log from successful manual rollback
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-010/rollback-auto-trigger.log`: Log from CD-triggered automatic rollback
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-010/circuit-breaker-test.log`: Log showing circuit breaker tripping at 3 rapid rollbacks
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-010/alembic-downgrade-review.txt`: Sample alembic downgrade SQL output from a safe downgrade
- `docs/setup-evidence/P10/STEP-P10-010/known-good-commits.json`: Sample known-good commit history file

#### Rollback

```bash
# Rollback is the feature itself — to disable, stop calling it
# The script is non-destructive; leaving it installed has zero impact
# To fully remove:
rm /home/guinevere/scripts/rollback.sh
rm /home/guinevere/config/known-good-commits.json
rm /home/guinevere/config/rollback-circuit.json
```

#### Troubleshooting

- **Issue:** Rollback itself fails — git checkout fails or health check still fails after rollback
  - **Solution:** SSH directly into the VPS. Manually inspect: `git log --oneline -5`, `systemctl status guinevere-*`, `journalctl -u guinevere-api -n 100`. If services are down, start them manually. If database is corrupted, restore from latest backup. This is the emergency path — the rollback script failing is a "wake Faiz up" event.

- **Issue:** Alembic downgrade is destructive (contains DROP TABLE/COLUMN)
  - **Solution:** The script skips automatic downgrade and logs a warning. Manually review `/tmp/alembic_downgrade.sql`. If the migration added a column (non-destructive), it is safe to leave it. If it dropped a column, you need the expand-contract pattern — the migration should have been a multi-step process (add new column, migrate data, drop old column in separate migration).

- **Issue:** Multiple rapid rollbacks trigger circuit breaker
  - **Solution:** The circuit breaker pauses CD for 10 minutes. Investigate the root cause of repeated failures — likely a broken commit on `main` that needs to be reverted upstream. Reset the circuit breaker manually: `echo '{"count":0,"window_start":""}' > /home/guinevere/config/rollback-circuit.json`.

- **Issue:** `requirements-freeze.txt` is stale or missing
  - **Solution:** Update P10-007 deploy script to generate `pip freeze > requirements-freeze.txt` after every successful `pip install`. If the file is missing, the rollback script falls back to `pip install -e "."`, which installs the latest versions from `pyproject.toml` — this may install different versions than the known-good deployment.

#### Notes

- Database rollback is the riskiest component. The script deliberately skips automatic `alembic downgrade` if the SQL preview contains DROP statements. Non-destructive migrations (add column, add table, add index) are safe to downgrade. Destructive migrations MUST use the expand-contract pattern: (1) deploy new column/table, (2) backfill data, (3) deploy code that reads both old and new, (4) deploy code that writes only new, (5) deploy migration that drops old column/table. Each step is a separate deploy, ensuring rollback never needs to restore dropped data.
- The circuit breaker resets after 10 minutes without a rollback. This prevents one bad commit from blocking all future deployments indefinitely.
- Rollback does NOT touch SOPS-encrypted secrets. If a deploy changed encrypted secrets, the rollback must also revert those files — this is left manual for safety (secrets changes are rare).
- Discord `/rollback` command integration (for manual trigger) is handled in P9-005 (Slash Commands batch) and should call this script directly.
